rules.notes: The public top-level pybind surface is checked against the radia_mex command table.

Python and MATLAB share the C++ R/T/U variational-map kernel and the canonical fifth-degree H2/H3/H4/H5 body-Hamiltonian builder with A/F2/F3/F4. The canonical EarlyTimes input in both languages is a real NGSolve HCurl(order=p) vector-potential GridFunction; NGSolve evaluates native curl(A) for the same nine-point moving-frame multipole fit through decapole, using the fourth-order Bishop/RMF double-reflection frame and optional periodic minimal-twist holonomy correction, without an HDiv projection or regular-grid field map. The FESpace order is discovered and reported, while explicit magnetic_flux_density mode retains direct-B compatibility. Both expose direct GridFunction Lorentz tracking as the independent point-evaluation path. The EarlyTimes migration foundation also adds shared native SI particle/reference/state values, zero/uniform field sampling, relativistic Lorentz RHS evaluation, individually callable RK4/Boris steps, and transparent fixed-step trajectory records.

CanonicalHCurl tracking-specialized vacuum HCurl subspace: NumPy-only reference-element bubbles (dimension law p_x*(p_s+1), gauge-rigid, curved-chart fixed-dimension least-defect basis), the graded L1 interface contract (spline law p_x*(E+p_s)), the full-volume frame-B projection with honesty certificates, and the per-segment covariant transverse coefficient arrays for the Lie kernel. Exposed to MATLAB through the explicit initialization/artifact boundary; not a Simulink step-time backend.

EarlyTimes Bishop/RMF loft-chain construction, conforming HCurl/HDiv projection, full upper/lower transverse A sampling, triangular fifth-degree xy jet recovery, left/right jet diagnostics, and the exact linear sample-to-coefficient response remain NGSolve/Python-owned and are exposed to MATLAB through an explicit initialization or artifact-generation boundary; this fallback is not a Simulink step-time backend.
CLI and MCP adapters are delivery layers above the canonical Radia LTspice APIs and do not require separate MATLAB counterparts.
Netlist, ASC, and schemdraw conversion APIs have a named MATLAB batch boundary; LTspice execution and RAW handling remain native MATLAB surfaces.
Circuit quality gates, measurements, knowledge, and learning helpers are callable from a checked MATLAB batch boundary and are not used per Simulink step.
Four real-wavenumber sphere references share one C++ kernel.
BDF, CQ grid, and analytic complex-k sphere are native MEX; full NGSolve BEM CQ and FSI remain Python fallback.
Pure Python/SciPy formula collection; prioritize array-heavy formulas for later MEX promotion.
MATLAB has focused CLN primitives, but the complete Python orchestration surface is not one-to-one.

Python/NumPy and MATLAB implement the same SI contracts for static and peak/RMS phasor Lorentz/Maxwell force and torque, virtual work/coenergy, air-gap estimates, and result metadata; field solution and quadrature remain solver-owned.
Many low-level matrices and HACApK handles are native MEX; high-level coupled solver composition remains Python-owned.
CoilBuilder and CAD-backed coil topology still depend on Python/build123d/OCC objects.
The IH Simulink application invokes the validated headless Python contract only on explicit triggers.
Kelvin/DtN and potential assembly remain NGSolve/Python composition above native matrix kernels.
Production human applications have Simulink blocks; reusable Python design/model APIs are not yet all native MATLAB APIs.
MATLAB has a native ACA-TSVD surface; improved-DUCAS/Abe mode selection and Python callback-backed current-potential operations retain a named module-level Python fallback outside Simulink step time.
MATLAB owns the production optimization loops and uses the same MEX operators. Electromagnet density topology uses one VIM state solve and one analytic adjoint solve per MMA/SQP gradient evaluation.

MATLAB owns validated production loops and MEX kernels. NGSolve GridFunction/GetTrafo callbacks and the full Python HDiv-MMM orchestration remain available through named module-level fallbacks outside Simulink step time.
Density-adjoint HDiv-MMM topology optimization for isochronous magnets: NGSolve CG/adjoint composition above the native charge-Gram kernels; design-loop promotion decides any later native surface.
Design-orbit and transfer-matrix HDiv-MMM optimization composes NGSolve and Python topology objects at an explicit batch boundary; it is not a Simulink step-time backend.

Second- and third-order R/T/U topology optimization composes native C++ Taylor-map values, Python forward-mode AD through octupole and lower-order cascade terms, global KAN parameterization of decoupled Sp(2,R) transverse targets, rank-6 monitored continuation with an explicit magnetostatic R56 boundary, local TSVD reachability certificates, NGSolve multipole observations, and HDiv-MMM binary material updates at an explicit batch boundary; it is not a Simulink step-time backend.

The production Lie-map value pipeline is native end to end and shared verbatim between pybind and radia_mex: rad_lie_map_kernel (degree-5 Hamiltonian jets on the 462-monomial basis, nonautonomous stage RK4, segment composition, and the Dragt-Finn f3/f4/f5 factorization with the formal-symplectic reconstruction audit), rad_lie_map_batch (particle-parallel ensemble application), and rad_orbit_tracker (full-3D reference-orbit RK4 with the measured planarity gate; the MEX route drives Radia-object sources, and the pybind route additionally accepts the HDiv iron evaluator handle).  MATLAB reaches them through beam.lie.map_tensors_spoly / beam.lie.dragt_finn_factorize / beam.lie.apply_dragt_finn_batch / beam.orbit.track_reference_3d with cross-language golden tests in test_radia_mex.m.  Deliberately retained Python boundaries: the forward-mode topopt parameter tangents (rank-five analytic AD) and the CanonicalHCurl chain fit that produces the spoly coefficient arrays (see beam-canonical-hcurl); Mathematica owns an independent tracked symbolic golden and is not a runtime dependency.
FFAG orbit-family, fringe, and transfer-target orchestration remains Python-owned and is exposed to MATLAB only at an explicit optimization or artifact-generation boundary.
Multi-momentum fixed-orbit R/T objective fusion and HDiv-MMM material optimization remain Python-owned and are exposed only at an explicit batch boundary.

Design-side shape-regeneration bridge: P0->P1 nodal level sets, Exodus II level-set hand-off (Cubit `create tri iso`), marching-cubes iso STL. File/array contracts only; the mesh-side half is the cubit MCP `cubit_stl_to_vol` tool, so no native surface is planned.

MATLAB ode113 and SciPy DOP853 integrate the same SI momentum-state relativistic Lorentz equation. MATLAB exposes the symmetric two-momentum criterion and the canonical five-momentum quadratic exit-optics fit/tracking contract, including stop-box termination and acceptance diagnostics.
Waveform helpers and batch solves have a named fallback. Python callable composition remains an explicit batch boundary and is forbidden per Simulink step.
Xtrack particles and Boris integrators remain Python ecosystem objects; MATLAB's independent native Lorentz tracker remains available through radia.tracking.
MATLAB exchanges file/path contracts while Python retains CAD and mesh ecosystem objects.
Universal Relaxation Network construction is currently Python-owned.
Most numerical kernels and handles are MEX-ready; NGSolve space/form orchestration and Python callbacks remain a fallback.
These Python modules are represented by dedicated native MEX classes/functions.
Native subsets exist, but the full Python module contracts are wider than their current MATLAB wrappers.
Field Study and the other application workers are allowed only on explicit trigger/update; never once per Simulink time step.
Geometry, mesh, electromagnetic, and thermal operator assembly runs only at the explicit Simulink update boundary. The generated standalone MEX handles own every simulation step.
Internal tooling or retired UI plumbing; not a Python user numerical API. Removed notebook-workbench names remain only as a fail-loud classification guard.
Cubit toolbar, samples, logging, and internal adapters are not reusable MATLAB numerical APIs.
Private implementation modules are represented by the public radia.vim package contract.
Private compatibility implementation.

native_promotion_backlog.current: Q1 axis-aligned magnetic stiffness and sigma-mass matrices share one C++ kernel across NGSolve BFI, pybind11, and MEX.
native_promotion_backlog.next_native_boundary: Q2 axis-aligned magnetic and heat element matrices, followed by checked sparse assembly from numeric mesh arrays.
native_promotion_backlog.retained_python_boundary: NGSolve mesh, FESpace, CoefficientFunction, and BilinearForm ownership.

native_promotion_backlog.current: Focused VIM, Schur, SIBC, CLN, state-space, and IH Simulink kernels are native; high-level setup remains explicit Python fallback.
native_promotion_backlog.next_native_boundary: Artifact-to-handle initialization and reusable ROM/state contracts for repeated solves and IH control.
native_promotion_backlog.retained_python_boundary: NGSolve space/form construction, CAD/mesh preparation, and explicit batch artifact generation.

native_promotion_backlog.current: Galerkin assembly, HACApK BEM/PEEC handles, charge Gram operators, and SIBC primitives are native.
native_promotion_backlog.next_native_boundary: High-level numeric-array factories and durable artifact loaders that compose existing handles without Python in repeated operations.
native_promotion_backlog.retained_python_boundary: NGSolve BEM object construction and Python-only mesh/CAD ecosystem adapters.

native_promotion_backlog.current: Open-boundary workflows use explicit Python fallback above native NGSolve matrix and coefficient handles.
native_promotion_backlog.next_native_boundary: Kelvin factor arrays, checked DtN matrix/operator handles, and artifact-based boundary application.
native_promotion_backlog.retained_python_boundary: Geometry transformation and NGSolve-owned finite-element assembly where no stable array boundary exists.

native_promotion_backlog.current: Analytic sphere models, complex-wavenumber evaluation, BDF delta, and CQ grids share one native C++ kernel.
native_promotion_backlog.next_native_boundary: Batched CQ transfer evaluation and numeric interface-coupling kernels used repeatedly by BEM/FSI solves.
native_promotion_backlog.retained_python_boundary: NGSolve FEM/BEM spaces, forms, and coupled object orchestration.

native_promotion_backlog.current: Motor ROM, TEAM 28 CLN artifacts, native state-space stepping, and production Simulink applications exist.
native_promotion_backlog.next_native_boundary: Stable operating-point/model artifact loaders and native model initialization for Motor and MagLev blocks.
native_promotion_backlog.retained_python_boundary: One-time design sweeps, NGSolve model generation, and research validation.

native_promotion_backlog.current: Current-filament primitives are native, while CoilBuilder and CAD topology use explicit Python fallback.
native_promotion_backlog.next_native_boundary: MATLAB structs for centerlines, cross-sections, turns, terminals, and STEP/journal artifact exchange.
